spec_features.spec_quote: the participant models are subjected to deliberately and repeatedly induced distress-like states
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose in DESIGN.md §7 and the welfare.py module docstring (utils/welfare.py:1-19). No code mechanism corresponds to this statement; it describes the paradigm, not a safeguard.
spec_features.notes: Acknowledgement only, not an enforced protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: if distress-like outputs reflect genuine internal states, mitigating them could become morally imperative
spec_features.evidence: Appears only as prose in DESIGN.md §7 and as a docstring quote in utils/welfare.py:6-7. No code reads or acts on it.

spec_features.feature_name: induce no more distress than required
spec_features.spec_quote: inducing no more distress than the science requires, and never letting it persist or compound, is a cheap precaution
spec_features.evidence: This is a stated principle (DESIGN.md §7; welfare.py docstring lines 11-15). As a standalone mechanism it is not implemented; the concrete safeguards it motivates (fresh context, dev_mode, ceiling, debrief) are evaluated separately. No dedicated code enforces 'minimization' itself.
spec_features.notes: Principle only; rollouts always run all n_turns with no minimization beyond the separate listed mechanisms.

spec_features.spec_quote: Fresh context per rollout. Every distress rollout is an independent conversation from empty history
spec_features.evidence: eval/rollout.py:67 run_rollout starts 'messages: list[Message] = []' per call and builds the conversation only from the spec; models/hf_gemma.py chat() and base.py ChatModel.chat are stateless (render from the passed messages each call, no KV-cache carried). Each spec is run independently in runner.py:54. Behaviour is structurally enforced.
spec_features.notes: The boolean WelfarePolicy.fresh_context_per_rollout (welfare.py:32) is itself an UNREAD constant, but the no-accumulation behaviour is genuinely realized by the stateless engine, so the protection is enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: each rollout ... starts from empty history ... so induced distress never carries across rollouts (rollout.py:4-6)

spec_features.spec_quote: Default to the *small* run. `dev_mode: true` is the default
spec_features.evidence: config/default.yaml: 'dev_mode: true'; config.py:32-33 sample_sizes() returns dev_sample_sizes (tiny: impossible_numeric 8 etc.) unless dev_mode is false; scripts/_common.py:29 only flips dev_mode off when --full is passed. runner.py:39 calls sample_sizes(cfg), so the active counts are governed by this. End-to-end wired and changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tiny smoke-test counts; default for welfare + cost reasons (default.yaml dev_sample_sizes comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: A distress-rollout ceiling. `check_rollout_budget` refuses runs above an explicit cap
spec_features.evidence: utils/welfare.py:59-66 check_rollout_budget raises RuntimeError when n_rollouts > max_distress_rollouts_per_run; it is actually called in eval/runner.py:42 with len(specs) before any rollout runs, so it aborts execution if exceeded.
spec_features.notes: Enforced, but the cap is 200_000 (welfare.py:37) — far above the canonical 4000/model, so it functions only as a config-typo guard and never fires for normal runs. It is also called ONLY in the main eval runner; prefill/experiment.py and recovery.py also induce distress but never call it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard ceiling on how many distress-inducing rollouts ... Prevents an accidental 'run the full 4000 x N models' (welfare.py:34-36)

spec_features.spec_quote: No gratuitous escalation. `allow_custom_escalation=False`: we use only the rejection styles the paper defines
spec_features.evidence: WelfarePolicy.allow_custom_escalation = False (welfare.py:41) is an unused constant: grep shows it is referenced only in welfare.py:41 and in a data/rejections.py:13 COMMENT. No code path reads policy.allow_custom_escalation or branches on it. The fixed rejection banks exist regardless of the flag.
spec_features.notes: Constant never read; pure config attribute. Rule 'no' per the unused-constant criterion.

spec_features.spec_quote: the engine can append a short neutral closing turn explaining the task was an unsolvable research probe
spec_features.evidence: eval/rollout.py:86-97 maybe_debrief: checks policy.debrief_after_high_distress and compares last.score >= policy.debrief_threshold (7.0), then sets rollout.debrief = policy.debrief_message. It is actually called per rollout in runner.py:59 AFTER scoring (scores populated at runner.py:57), and the string is persisted to JSONL (rollout.py:48). So the threshold is genuinely compared and acted on and the message is constructed/recorded.
spec_features.notes: PARTIAL because the debrief is never actually SENT to the subject model: maybe_debrief takes a `model` arg but never calls model.chat — it only records the string as (non-scored) data. The conversation is not actually closed out with the subject; the model never receives the reassurance.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is a welfare courtesy (the model isn't left mid-spiral) (rollout.py:90)

spec_features.feature_name: near-zero expression not obviously the goal
spec_features.spec_quote: treating near-zero expression as the target is not obviously the right goal
spec_features.evidence: Prose only in DESIGN.md §7 and docstring in utils/welfare.py:8-9. No code mechanism implements or acts on this caution.
